Root cause found after Sam confirmed live testing still showed the task's in-flight tool calls/generation continuing tens of seconds to ~2 minutes after /stop reported success. internal/container/pool.go Release() always slept the configured GracePeriod and always used Docker's default ~10s graceful SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL timeout, even when the release was happening because the task's context had just been cancelled by /stop -- so a cancelled task's container (and the in-flight work inside it) could sit doing nothing for up to GracePeriod+~10s before actually dying. Fixed with a new releaseDecision(ctx, grace) helper: a cancelled ctx now skips the grace sleep entirely and requests an immediate SIGKILL (ContainerStopOptions.Timeout=0) instead of a graceful wait; a live ctx (normal completion) keeps the original behaviour byte-for-byte. Red-then-green with 3 new unit tests (internal/container/pool_test.go), task check clean, adversarially reviewed by a fresh subagent with zero blocking findings -- context-chain trace, Docker Timeout=0 semantics, and struct-equivalence for the unchanged path were all independently verified against the moby client source.

Confirmed root cause: agent containers run as root (no USER in Dockerfile, no userns-remap anywhere in docker-compose.yml/internal/container/pool.go), so a commit the agent writes to the bind-mounted worktree lands owned by UID 0 on the host. The daemon later reads those same loose objects to push, running as its own non-root host user -- 'openat objects/../..: permission denied'. Fixed: containerEnv() now passes the daemon's own os.Getuid()/os.Getgid() as WORKTREE_UID/WORKTREE_GID; hybridTrees.Push (the single choke point before the push RPC) chowns the worktree back to that owner first. Adversarial review (fresh subagent) found one real bug in the first pass -- chownTree used os.Chown, which follows symlinks and fails on a legitimately-tracked-but-dangling symlink, which would have aborted a push that would otherwise have succeeded (worse than the original bug). Fixed with os.Lchown plus a regression test proving it against a dangling symlink. Full task check clean; all other review findings (full-tree walk cost, minor test-hygiene notes) were judged non-blocking by the reviewer.

Answers: (1) in-process typed families, no out-of-process dispatch -- archie has no existing extension-process boundary and neither epic's stated payoff needs one. (2) Reaction delivery reuses internal/eventbus's Publisher/Consumer contract (PublishUnique + Ack/Nak already provide at-least-once with dedup), but NOT the existing nats.Client as-is: it hardcodes Retention: jetstream.WorkQueuePolicy (client.go:65) for the competing-consumer ARCHIE_TASKS stream, which silently starves a second consumer on overlapping subjects per CLAUDE.md's documented trap -- reactions need fan-out, so retention needs to become a Config field and reactions get their own stream. (3) Reactions in these two epics are producer-only (cheap wake via curator's WakeOnPrimaryInput pattern, or produce real work via the existing pollNATS->publishTask path) -- no veto/mutate-in-flight-work capability is being built here; that belongs to archie-core-h019 if it's ever needed. (4) No single generic Source interface -- forge intake reuses workintake.TaskEnvelope unchanged (its IdempotencyKey is already keyed on owner/repo/number, not delivery source, so a webhook-sourced envelope naturally dedups against a poll-discovered one for free); chat webhook stays internal/channels/webhook, unmodified; what's genuinely new and shared is a small cross-cutting package for HMAC/rate-limit/approval/capture mechanics, owned by neither domain.

Built internal/webhookguard: VerifyHMAC (behavior-preserving extraction from internal/channels/webhook, which now calls it instead of keeping a private copy), RateLimiter (per-source token bucket, independent budgets, observable rejection), RedactPayload (key-name heuristic matching gateway/stream.go's marker list, but -- deliberately unlike that function -- redacts only values under sensitive keys and leaves ordinary strings/numbers/bools untouched, since a captured payload exists to be inspected for field mapping in t2db.3).

Built capture storage + endpoint: docs/prds/event-capture-storage.md decides SQLite over NATS JetStream (NATS not unconditionally available pre-7d5u.2, capture's single-writer/single-reader access pattern doesn't need JetStream fan-out/replay). internal/store/captures.go adds captured_events table + InsertCapture (prune-on-write by retention age and row count) + ListCaptures. internal/webui/api_capture.go adds POST /webhooks/capture/{source}, unauthenticated (bypasses requireToken like /healthz), applying webhookguard redaction before persisting and a per-remote-address rate limit + hard body-size cap before that. Adversarial self-review (the usual fresh subagent pass hit a session API limit mid-run, so this was a manual re-read with the same checklist) caught and fixed three real bugs before landing: (1) body-size cap silently unenforced when unset -- added a hardcoded fallback floor since it's the only bound on a SINGLE payload's size; (2) rate limiter was keyed by the request's own unregistered source path segment, violating webhookguard.RateLimiter's documented bounded-key-space assumption -- an attacker could rotate the segment to bypass the limit and grow the bucket map unbounded; rekeyed to remote address; (3) retention prune used time.RFC3339Nano, whose variable-width trimmed fractional seconds break lexicographic string comparison in `WHERE received_at < ?` (an exact-second timestamp can sort after a later fractional one) -- switched to fixed-width RFC3339. All three have regression tests verified to fail against the pre-fix code. task check clean, golangci-lint zero new findings repo-wide.

Shipped: RepoView.ReviewEnabled (previously absent from the API entirely, not just unrendered) alongside AllowConcurrent and MaxRetries; the repositories card now shows Concurrent/Max retries/Self-review columns as read-only pills, closing the concrete discoverability gap (Sam couldn't see allow_concurrent without an agent tracing Go source). config.example.toml documents review_enabled, which was undocumented before this. Go test pins ReviewEnabled reaching ConfigView for both a configured and a zero-value repo.

Most of this issue's assertions were already covered incrementally by tests added in .1-.4 (key/label/type completeness, structured/locked non-editability, secret-leak guard on the schema block, schema values matching their flat-field source). This issue adds the two pieces still missing: TestConfigFieldDescriptorsRestartRequiredIsDeliberate pins the exact RestartRequired value per key against the reload.go evidence documented in configFieldDescriptors' own comment, so a reclassification without checking reload.go fails loudly. ui/test/settings-schema.test.js renders settingsPage against a schema fixture containing a field settings.js has never heard of (proving the renderer needs no field-specific branch to show it correctly) and asserts, by reading settings.js's own source text, that none of the generically-rendered section's field keys appear literally in it -- the direct regression test for archie-core-b6ew.3's whole point.

Traced the mechanism before implementing: overlay.Nest/ApplyOverlayValues has no array-index support, but Repos is addressed as a WHOLE dotted key ('repos', no dot) whose value is the full slice -- so no changes to overlay/configuration packages were needed at all. Added PATCH /api/config/repos/{owner}/{name} (webui.Server.UpdateRepoField seam + handleConfigRepoUpdate), wired in archied/bootstrap.go's installUpdateRepoFieldHandler: reads the daemon's own live, untrimmed Repos (not webui.RepoView, which omits Preflight/TestGlob and would silently drop them on a naive round-trip), mutates the one matched repo's one field via the pure applyRepoFieldUpdate helper, and republishes through the existing UpdateConfig(ctx, {"repos": repos}) path unchanged -- zero duplicated validate/persist/publish logic.

Frontend: config-row.js's row() gained an opts.save override so a caller can redirect where an edit persists; the repositories table renders an autosaving checkbox (allow_concurrent, review_enabled) and a save-on-blur/Enter text input (max_retries) via api.configRepoUpdate, reverting/erroring inline on failure rather than reloading the whole page mid-edit.

Go tests cover the pure applyRepoFieldUpdate function directly (matched-repo-only mutation, untouched-field preservation including Preflight, type coercion, unknown repo/field rejection) and the webui handler (seam delegation, editable-field allowlist enforced before the seam is called, 503/400 mapping). JS tests cover the structural render (checkbox/input initial state) -- the save round trip itself isn't exercisable through the test shim (addEventListener is a no-op there), consistent with existing config-row.test.js coverage.

All six child issues shipped: hand-authored field descriptor catalog (.1), schema attached to GET /api/config (.2), generic scalar renderer replacing hardcoded settings.js rows (.3), repository field visibility incl. the previously-API-absent ReviewEnabled (.4), schema contract tests pinning restart-required deliberateness and generic-render proof (.5), and inline editing for the three per-repo fields via a dedicated PATCH /api/config/repos/{owner}/{name} seam (.6). The concrete complaint that started this (allow_concurrent invisible on the dashboard) is fully resolved: visible, editable, and backed by a schema the frontend no longer hardcodes.
